A new test which can predict with 100 per cent accuracy

This is where they lost me.

I couldn't find the original published article, but I think they might be referring to this.

If 100 patients known to have a disease were tested, and 43 test positive, then the test has 43% sensitivity. If 100 with no disease are tested and 96 return a negative result, then the test has 96% specificity.

Basically, the test in the article may have a high sensitivity, but a low specificity, detecting 100% of the patients who will develop cancer, but also returning a high number of false positives.

Thank you. Of course it's also possible that they're saying it can predict with 100 per cent accuracy but doesn't always...

Or maybe, maybe 100% is a rounded figure – but even something at or above 99.5% seems dubious in this field.
Wonderful post! This kind of issue is easily missed by those without enough knowledge of clinical trials.
